stemBlocks.value: A = (1 2 / 3 1), x is the column vector (x / y) and b = (7 / 11), with Ax = b. (a) Write down the TWO simultaneous equations represented by the matrix equation. (b) Determine the values of x and y. (c) Check the solution by matrix multiplication.
Think first: Each row of A multiplied into the column (x / y) produces one ordinary equation.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p200-q14 from workbook page 200.

solutionSteps.instruction: Multiply row 1 of A into the column (x / y) and set it equal to the top entry of b.
Do the same with row 2 of A and the bottom entry of b.
Rearrange the second equation and substitute into the first.
Substitute x = 3 back to find y.
Multiply A by the solution column to check.

contentBlocks.value: Result: (7 / 11) = b, so the solution is correct

strategyBlocks.value: Expand Ax row by row to get two equations, solve them by substitution, then multiply A by the solution vector to confirm it gives b.

whyThisWorks.value: The row-by-column rule turns each row of the coefficient matrix into the left-hand side of one equation, so a whole system can be packed into a single matrix statement. Solving is then ordinary algebra. Multiplying back is the fastest possible check because it re-derives both equations at once.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing the equations from the columns of A instead of the rows.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing the equations from the columns of A instead of the rows.
Avoid this: Sign slips when expanding 2(11 − 3x).

commonErrors.misconception: Finding x and forgetting to substitute back for y.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Finding x and forgetting to substitute back for y.

examTip.value: After solving a matrix system, always feed your answer back through Ax — it takes seconds and catches nearly every arithmetic slip.
